body: It looks like this isn't actually based on the umask. There are other machines and users with the same umask that aren't getting this.

This isn't caused by my umask:
```
[manybubbles@localhost elasticsearch]$ ./gradlew -p distribution clean
...
[manybubbles@localhost elasticsearch]$ umask 0022
[manybubbles@localhost elasticsearch]$ umask
0022
[manybubbles@localhost elasticsearch]$ ./gradlew -p qa/vagrant/ packagingTest
...
# Expected privileges: 644, found 664 [/usr/share/elasticsearch/modules/lang-painless/antlr4-runtime-4.5.3.jar]
```

I was wrong about it not being my umask. If I `git clean -xdf` after setting my umask to `0022` then I get *further*. The tests still fail because my clone of elasticsearch has `README.textile` as `664` rather than `644`. I *think* the umask that you had when you cloned Elasticsearch influences that one.

issue.title: Force stable file modes for built packages

labels.name: :Delivery/Packaging
labels.description: RPM and deb packaging, tar and zip archives, shell and batch scripts

repository.name: elasticsearch
repository.description: Free and Open Source, Distributed, RESTful Search Engine

issue.body:
If you have an unusual umask (e.g., 0002) and clone the GitHub repository then files that we stick into our packages like the README.textile and the license will have a file mode of 0664 on disk yet we expect them to be 0644. Additionally, the same thing happens with compiled artifacts like JARs. We try to set a default file mode yet it does not seem to take everywhere. This commit adds explicit file modes in some places that we were relying on the defaults to ensure that the built artifacts have a consistent file mode regardless of the underlying build host.

Closes #30799

issue.title: stable filemode for zip distributions

labels.name: :Delivery/Packaging
labels.description: RPM and deb packaging, tar and zip archives, shell and batch scripts

repository.name: elasticsearch
repository.description: Free and Open Source, Distributed, RESTful Search Engine

issue.body:
Applies default file and directory permissions to zip distributions
similar to how they're set for the tar distributions. Previously zip
distributions would retain permissions they had on the build host's
working tree, which could vary depending on its umask

For #30799
